subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should OpenClaw change managed npm override propagation for third-party plugin roots, add Express 4-specific install validation, or keep the current policy that plugin packages must pin their own conflicting dependency graph?
rationale: This choice affects the security/reproducibility purpose of host overrides, third-party plugin dependency ownership, and whether OpenClaw should repair or only diagnose dependency conflicts outside core.

options.title: Scope managed overrides
options.body: Filter or scope host overrides so plugin-owned dependency graphs can satisfy Express 4 while OpenClaw keeps path-to-regexp 8.x for its own Express 5/router stack.

options.title: Add validator only
options.body: Detect Express 4 plus missing path-to-regexp 0.1.x compatibility during install and fail with a clear operator/plugin-author action, without changing override propagation.

options.title: Leave to plugin authors
options.body: Keep current managed-root override behavior and require affected plugin packages to ship their own override or migrate to Express 5.

recommendation.title: Scope managed overrides
recommendation.body: Filter or scope host overrides so plugin-owned dependency graphs can satisfy Express 4 while OpenClaw keeps path-to-regexp 8.x for its own Express 5/router stack.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc authored the managed override propagation and current workspace override metadata paths most directly involved in the policy choice.
